mainTopic: The fast-day blessings, and the wine and haircut rules for כהנים on duty in the בית המקדש, then and nowadays
overview: This amud covers the extra blessings said on a public fast and the special rules for the כהנים on duty in the בית המקדש. First the גמרא explains why some people swap the endings 'crying' and 'prayer' between the blessings for שמואל and אליהו. Then it explains why יונה comes before דוד: the last blessing must end with 'מרחם על הארץ'. סומכוס ends that blessing with 'משפיל הרמים' instead. Next, a ברייתא explains why the אנשי משמר may drink wine only at night, while the בית אב on duty may never drink. From this, a כהן today avoids wine for a day, a week, or a whole year, depending on how much he knows about his turn. רבי says that by this logic wine should be forbidden forever, but the long חורבן makes that impossible, and אביי says כהנים today drink following רבי. The גמרא then explains the ban on haircuts and laundering during the week of service. It gives the haircut schedules of a מלך, a כהן גדול and a כהן הדיוט, learning the thirty days for a כהן from נזיר through the word 'פרע'. Finally it asks why כהנים do not keep this rule today. The challenge from רבי's view on wine continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing a teaching: only on three occasions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a teaching from the previous page. It lists the only times the practice applies: ראש השנה, the יובל year, and a time of war.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only on ראש השנה, in יובל years, and in a time of war.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of a teaching that started on the previous page. It finishes a list of the only three occasions when that practice is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main rule was stated just before this line. Here we only get its exceptions: ראש השנה, the יובל year, and wartime. After this, the גמרא moves on to a new piece of the משנה.

phrases.english: only on Rosh HaShana,
and in Jubilee years, and in a time of war.
phrases.notes: For the יובל, this means the יום כיפור of the Jubilee year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a teaching begun on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The practice applies only on ראש השנה, in the יובל year, and in wartime.

steps.title: Some people swap the endings for שמואל and אליהו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the first blessing ('He Who answered אברהם'). Then it brings a ברייתא: some people switch the endings 'crying' and 'prayer' between the blessings of שמואל and אליהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that for the first blessing he says 'He Who answered אברהם', and so on. A ברייתא teaches that some people swap the endings: they put 'crying' with אליהו and 'prayer' with שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's list of fast-day blessings. It brings a ברייתא saying that some people swap the endings of two of those blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the blessing about שמואל ends 'שומע צעקה' (Who hears crying). The blessing about אליהו ends 'שומע תפלה' (Who hears prayer). This ברייתא reports a practice that switches the two endings, and that sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.english: For the first [blessing] he says:
He Who answered Abraham, etc.
It was taught: some switch
"crying" for Elijah, and "prayer" for Samuel.
phrases.notes: In the משנה it is the other way around: שמואל gets 'crying' and אליהו gets 'prayer'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the endings of the fast-day blessings in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some people end the אליהו blessing with 'crying' and the שמואל blessing with 'prayer'.

steps.title: Where is 'crying' written about אליהו?
steps.stepSummary: Both 'prayer' and 'crying' are written about שמואל, so either ending fits him. About אליהו, only 'prayer' is written. So how can his blessing end with 'crying'?
steps.simpleTranslation: With שמואל there is no problem: the פסוקים use both 'prayer' and 'crying' for him. But with אליהו, 'prayer' is written and 'crying' is not. So how can we end his blessing with 'crying'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the swap in the ברייתא. It agrees that שמואל can get either word, but asks how 'crying' can be linked to אליהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each blessing's ending should match how the פסוקים describe that person's prayer. For שמואל, both words appear in the פסוקים, so the swap is fine for him. For אליהו, the word 'crying' never appears, so giving him that ending seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (the first half of a challenge)

phrases.english: Granted, regarding Samuel —
it is written about him "prayer"
and it is written about him "crying."
But regarding Elijah —
prayer is written, crying is not written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the swap reported in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of ending the אליהו blessing with 'crying'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A blessing's ending should match the פסוקים, and the word 'crying' is never written about אליהו.

steps.title: 'Answer me, ה׳, answer me' is a cry
steps.stepSummary: אליהו's words 'ענני ה׳ ענני' are a form of crying out, even though the word 'crying' is not used.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אליהו said 'Answer me, ה׳, answer me,' that was a way of crying out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. אליהו's repeated plea, 'answer me, answer me', counts as crying out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'צעקה' does not need to appear in the פסוק. The style of אליהו's words, an urgent and repeated plea, is itself a cry. So the swap in the ברייתא has a basis in the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: A way of speaking / an expression of

steps.whatToRemember: Both endings can work for either prophet: שמואל has both words in the פסוקים, and אליהו's 'ענני ה׳ ענני' counts as a cry.

phrases.english: "Answer me, ה׳, answer me"
is an expression of crying.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲנֵנִי ה׳ עֲנֵנִי לְשׁוֹן צְעָקָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a פסוק: the style of the words counts as 'crying'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the actual word 'צעקה' would count, and it never appears about אליהו.
steps.terutzMaskana: אליהו's repeated plea is itself a cry, so the 'crying' ending can go with him.

steps.title: Why is יונה placed before דוד?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה puts יונה in the sixth blessing and דוד in the seventh. Since יונה lived after דוד and שלמה, why does he come first?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says that for the sixth blessing he says 'He Who answered יונה', and for the seventh, 'He Who answered דוד'. But יונה lived after דוד and שלמה, so why is he mentioned first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. It asks why the order breaks history by putting יונה before דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the list seems to follow the order of history (אברהם, then later figures). יונה came after דוד and שלמה, so the order here looks strange. The גמרא wants to know the reason.

phrases.english: For the sixth he says:
He Who answered Jonah, etc.
For the seventh he says:
He Who answered David, etc.

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי יוֹנָה בָּתַר דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Now since Jonah lived after David and Solomon,
what is the reason he puts him first?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי יוֹנָה בָּתַר דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new part of the משנה: the sixth and seventh blessings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה lists יונה before דוד and שלמה, against the order of history.

steps.title: The last blessing must end 'מרחם על הארץ'
steps.stepSummary: דוד and שלמה come last because the series has to end with 'Who has mercy on the Land', and that ending fits them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the last blessing is meant to end with 'Who has mercy on the Land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the order is set by how the series must end. The ending 'מרחם על הארץ' goes with דוד and שלמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is not about history. It is about matching each ending to the right story. The closing words 'מרחם על הארץ' fit דוד and שלמה, who were kings of the Land and prayed for it, so their blessing is placed last.

keyTerms.meaning: Who has mercy on the Land

phrases.english: Because he wants to conclude
"Who has mercy on the Land."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The order follows the endings: the final ending, 'מרחם על הארץ', fits דוד and שלמה, so they come last.

steps.title: סומכוס's different ending for the last blessing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that סומכוס ended the final blessing with 'Blessed is He Who humbles the exalted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught in the name of סומכוס: the last blessing ends 'Blessed is He Who humbles the exalted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different opinion about how to end the last blessing. סומכוס's ending is 'משפיל הרמים', not 'מרחם על הארץ'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This offers another way to close the series. Instead of mercy on the Land, the ending praises ה׳ for bringing down the proud.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose opinions are often quoted in ברייתות
Who humbles the exalted / brings down the proud

steps.whatToRemember: The order of the fast-day blessings follows their endings, not history. The last blessing ends 'מרחם על הארץ', or 'משפיל הרמים' according to סומכוס.

phrases.english: It was taught: in the name of Sumakhos they said:
"Blessed [is He] Who humbles the exalted."
phrases.notes: This is how סומכוס ends that final blessing instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different ending for the final blessing discussed in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to סומכוס, the final blessing ends 'ברוך משפיל הרמים'.

steps.title: The משנה's line about the priestly watch during the first fasts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: on the first three fasts, אנשי משמר fast but do not finish the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first three fasts, the men of the priestly watch fast but do not complete the fast, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new section by quoting a line from the משנה. It is setting up a ברייתא that explains the wine rules for כהנים on duty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion about the order of the ברכות is over. Now the focus moves to the כהנים serving in the בית המקדש, and the ברייתא that follows explains why their rules are different.

keyTerms.meaning: The men of the priestly watch, the group of כהנים whose week it is to serve in the בית המקדש
They complete the fast, until nightfall

phrases.english: On the first three fasts
the men of the priestly watch fast
but do not complete the fast, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלֹשׁ תַּעֲנִיּוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר מִתְעַנִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the discussion of the fast-day ברכות ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first three fasts, אנשי משמר fast but do not complete the fast.

steps.title: Why the priestly watch may drink wine at night but not by day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why אנשי משמר may drink wine at night but not during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: For what reason did they say that the men of the priestly watch may drink wine at night but not during the day?
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא asks for the reason behind a rule in the משנה. It is setting up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אנשי משמר are not the group serving that specific day, so why limit them at all? And if they are limited, why only by day? The question asks why the rule splits between day and night.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא
For what reason did they say? This asks for the reason behind a rule

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
For what reason did they say
that the men of the priestly watch are permitted to drink wine
at night but not during the day?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר מוּתָּרִין לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה's wine rule for אנשי משמר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason אנשי משמר are allowed wine at night but not by day.

steps.title: They might be called in to help during the day
steps.stepSummary: By day, the work may become too heavy for that day's בית אב, and the rest of the משמר might be called in to help.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because perhaps the service will become too heavy for the men of the family group, and they will come and help them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: during the day, the rest of the משמר might be needed to help, so they must stay ready to serve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each day only one בית אב serves, but on a busy day it may need help from the rest of the משמר. A כהן who drank wine may not do the עבודה, so the backup group must stay sober while the work is going on. At night the work is lighter, so they are not expected to be called in, and wine is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The service becomes heavy or burdensome
The family group serving on that specific day

phrases.english: Lest the service become burdensome
on the men of the family group,
and they will come and help them.
phrases.notes: "They" are the rest of the משמר, who might be called in, so they cannot be drunk.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא תִּכְבַּד הָעֲבוֹדָה עַל אַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By day the משמר may be called to help the בית אב with the service, so they must stay sober. At night there is no such need.

steps.title: Why the day's family group may never drink
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why אנשי בית אב may not drink wine by day or by night.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what reason did they say that the men of the family group may not drink, neither by day nor by night?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a second question, this time about the stricter rule for the בית אב serving that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the משמר, the בית אב is banned from wine even at night. The question asks why it gets this complete ban.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither by day nor by night

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ אַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב
phrases.english: For what reason did they say that the men of the family group
may not drink, neither by day nor by night?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ אַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב לֹא בַּיּוֹם וְלֹא בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משמר's partial ban to the בית אב's full ban.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the בית אב is banned from wine both day and night.

steps.title: They are always busy with the service
steps.stepSummary: The בית אב is always busy with the עבודה, so it may never drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are always busy with the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the family group on duty is busy with the service all the time, both day and night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משמר is only a possible backup. The בית אב is the group actually doing the work, including tasks at night. So the concern about wine applies to them at all hours.
steps.whatToRemember: משמר: no wine by day, because they might be called in to help. בית אב: no wine at any time, because they are always serving.

phrases.english: Because they are constantly engaged in the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בית אב is constantly engaged in the עבודה, so wine is never allowed for them.

steps.title: A priest who knows his exact day may not drink wine that day
steps.stepSummary: From this, חכמים rule that a כהן who knows both his משמר and his בית אב may not drink wine on his family's day.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: Any כהן who knows his watch and his family group's turn, and knows his ancestors were established there, may not drink wine that entire day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now applies the reasoning to כהנים today, after the חורבן. This is the first of three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is the same: a כהן who might be called to serve must be sober. If the בית המקדש is rebuilt, a כהן who knows his exact day could be called that day. So he avoids wine only on that one day.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said. A new ruling learned from what came before

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a בית המקדש rule into a rule for every generation, based on the hope that the עבודה could return at any time.

phrases.english: From here they said:
Any priest who knows his priestly watch
and the turn of his family group,
and knows that his ancestors' family was established there,

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן כׇּל אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם.
phrases.english: is forbidden to drink wine that entire day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁמַּכִּיר מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical ruling for today from the reasoning of steps 10 and 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who knows both his משמר and his בית אב may not drink wine on his family's day.

steps.title: A priest who knows only his week may not drink all that week
steps.stepSummary: If he knows his משמר but not his בית אב, he may not drink wine for that whole week.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he knows his watch but not his family group's turn, and knows his ancestors were established there, he may not drink wine that whole week.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second case. He knows less, so the ban lasts longer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He knows which week is his, but not which day of that week. Since any day of that week could be his, he must avoid wine all week.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means a week, not the day of שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Here שבת does not mean the seventh day. It means the whole week of his משמר.

phrases.english: In the case of one who knows his priestly watch

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַכִּיר מִשְׁמֶרֶת בֵּית אָב שֶׁלּוֹ,
phrases.english: but does not know the turn of his family group,
and knows that his ancestors' family was established there,

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן כׇּל אוֹתָהּ שַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: he is forbidden to drink wine that entire week.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַכִּיר מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ וְאֵין מַכִּיר מִשְׁמֶרֶת בֵּית אָב שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the ban to a week when he knows less.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he knows his משמר but not his בית אב, he may not drink wine for that whole week.

steps.title: A priest who knows neither may not drink all year
steps.stepSummary: If he knows neither his משמר nor his בית אב, he may not drink wine the whole year.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he knows neither his watch nor his family group's turn, but knows his ancestors were established there, he may not drink wine the whole year.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third and final case. With no information at all about his turn, the ban covers the entire year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every day of the year might be his turn, so every day he must stay ready. The less he knows, the longer the ban: a day, then a week, then a year.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban grows as his knowledge shrinks. Knows his day: one day. Knows only his week: one week. Knows neither: the whole year.

phrases.english: If he does not know his priestly watch
or the turn of his family group,
but knows that his ancestors' family was established there,
he is forbidden to drink wine the whole year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ מַכִּיר מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ וּמִשְׁמֶרֶת בֵּית אָב שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-case series with the widest ban.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כהן today must avoid wine whenever he might be the one called to serve: one day, one week, or the whole year, depending on what he knows.

steps.title: רבי: By Logic Wine Should Be Forbidden Forever, But It Cannot Be
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the reasoning of the ברייתא leads to a total ban on wine for all כהנים, but the long destruction of the בית המקדש makes such a ban unworkable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: I say it should be forbidden to drink wine forever. But what can I do? His ruin is what fixes things for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי pushes the last rule of the ברייתא (a כהן who doesn't know his משמר may never drink) one step further. Then he explains why we cannot actually rule that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry is that the בית המקדש could be rebuilt any day, then every כהן should always be ready to serve, so no כהן could ever drink wine. But the בית המקדש has been destroyed for so long that this ban cannot be kept up. The very damage, the long חורבן, is what lets the ban be relaxed.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה
his repair is his ruin; the bad situation is what brings the leniency

phrases.english: Rabbi says: I say:
it is forbidden to drink wine forever,
but what can I do,
since his fixing is his ruin.
phrases.notes: Literally 'his fixing is his ruin.' The very sad fact, the בית המקדש lying in ruins so long, is what lets the כהן drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the strictest rule of step 15 and extends its logic to every כהן at all times, then pulls back for practical reasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In theory every כהן should never drink wine, but because the חורבן has lasted so long, the ban is not enforced.

steps.title: אביי: Today's כהנים Drink Wine Following רבי
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whose opinion today's כהנים rely on when they drink wine, and answers: רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Like whom do כהנים drink wine nowadays? Like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes the wine discussion by naming which opinion the practice of his day follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's rule would forbid a כהן who doesn't know his משמר from drinking all year, and most כהנים no longer know their משמר. So the fact that כהנים drink wine shows they follow רבי's point that the long חורבן makes the ban unworkable.

keyTerms.meaning: like whom? according to whose opinion?

steps.whatToRemember: Strict logic would forbid every כהן from drinking wine, but because the חורבן has lasted so long, practice follows רבי and כהנים drink today.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In accordance with whom do priests drink wine nowadays?
In accordance with Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the current practice to רבי's view from step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: כהנים drink wine nowadays based on רבי.

steps.title: The משנה: No Haircuts or Laundering During the Week of Service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the אנשי משמר and אנשי מעמד may not cut hair or launder during their week, except on Thursday in honor of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The men of the משמר and the men of the מעמד may not cut their hair or wash their clothes. On Thursday they are allowed, in honor of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and quotes it. This sets up the next question about the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new rule about grooming. All week long the משמר and מעמד may not get haircuts or launder. Thursday is the exception, so that they look and dress properly for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the כהנים on duty in the בית המקדש that week
the Israelites linked to that week's משמר
to cut hair and to launder clothes

phrases.english: The members of the priestly watch and the members of the non-priestly watch
are forbidden to cut their hair and to launder,
but on Thursday they are permitted
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה after the wine discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משמר and מעמד may not cut hair or launder during their week, except on Thursday for שבת.

steps.title: Why Ban Haircuts and Laundering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה forbids haircuts and laundering. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being clean and well-groomed seems like a good thing, so it is not obvious why grooming would be forbidden during the week of service.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule quoted in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the משמר and מעמד may not cut hair or launder during their week.

steps.title: So They Won't Arrive Messy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the ban pushes them to groom before their week, so they don't start their service looking unkempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: So that they will not come into their משמר looking messy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: the ban makes sure they get haircuts and wash their clothes ahead of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since they know they cannot groom during the week, they will groom before it starts. The ban is really aimed at the days before the service, so that they come in looking neat.
steps.confusionAlert: The ban is not saying that grooming is bad. It is a way to make sure they groom BEFORE their week, so they start looking neat.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
so that they will not enter their watch
when they are unkempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנְסוּ לְמִשְׁמַרְתָּם כְּשֶׁהֵן מְנֻוּוֹלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban makes them groom beforehand so they do not start their service looking unkempt.

steps.title: ברייתא: How Often the מלך, כהן גדול, and כהן הדיוט Cut Their Hair
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives three haircut schedules: a מלך every day, a כהן גדול every Friday, and a כהן הדיוט every thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A מלך cuts his hair every day. A כהן גדול cuts his hair every Friday. A regular כהן cuts his hair once every thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא about haircuts. It sets up three questions that come next, one about each schedule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic of grooming for service leads to a list of three levels. The higher the person's honor, the more often he cuts his hair. The גמרא will now explain each rule.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A king cuts his hair every day,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל — מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: a High Priest, from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve,
a common priest, once every thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֶלֶךְ מִסְתַּפֵּר בְּכׇל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the related topic of haircuts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מלך cuts his hair daily, a כהן גדול weekly on Friday, and a כהן הדיוט every thirty days.

steps.title: Why Does the מלך Cut His Hair Every Day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the daily haircut of the מלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מלך cuts his hair every day. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the ברייתא, beginning with the מלך. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A daily haircut is unusual, so the גמרא wants a source or a reason for it.

phrases.english: A king cuts his hair every day:
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֶלֶךְ מִסְתַּפֵּר בְּכׇל יוֹם — מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the first rule of the ברייתא in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a מלך cuts his hair every day.

steps.title: The King Must Be Seen in His Beauty
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר זבדא brings a פסוק: 'Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר זבדא said: The פסוק says, 'Your eyes will see the king in his beauty.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק showing that a מלך must always look his best.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes people seeing the king in his beauty. Since he must always appear that way, he gets a haircut every day.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא, אָמַר קְרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said: The verse states:
"Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: מֶלֶךְ בְּיׇפְיוֹ תֶּחֱזֶינָה עֵינֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פסוק teaches that the king must be seen in his beauty.

steps.title: Why Does the כהן גדול Cut His Hair Every Friday?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the weekly Friday haircut of the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן גדול cuts his hair every Friday. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second rule in the ברייתא. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why exactly once a week, and why on Friday? The גמרא looks for what makes Friday special for the כהן גדול.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: A High Priest, from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve:
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת — מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the second rule of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the כהן גדול cuts his hair every Friday.

steps.title: A New משמר Arrives Each Week
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק explains that the משמרות change every week, so the כהן גדול grooms for each new group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יצחק said: Because the משמרות are renewed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the Friday haircut by pointing to the weekly change of משמרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each week a new group of כהנים comes on duty. The כהן גדול cuts his hair just before the change so that every new משמר sees him looking fresh.

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said:
Since the watches are renewed.
phrases.notes: A new משמר takes over each week, so the כהן גדול should look fresh for each new group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משמרות change weekly, so the כהן גדול grooms to greet each new group.

steps.title: Where Do We Learn Thirty Days for a Regular כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the thirty-day haircut rule for a כהן הדיוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: A regular כהן cuts his hair once every thirty days. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the third rule. This time it asks for a source, not just a reason. This sets up the derivation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number thirty is very specific. That suggests it comes from a פסוק, so the גמרא asks 'מנלן' (from where?).

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know this?

phrases.english: A common priest, once every thirty days:
From where do we derive this?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט אַחַת לִשְׁלשִׁים יוֹם — מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the third rule of the ברייתא, this time looking for a source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the thirty-day haircut rule for a כהן הדיוט.

steps.title: גזירה שוה of 'פרע': Learning Thirty Days from a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The word 'פרע' appears both for כהנים and for a נזיר. Since a נזיר's growth is thirty days, a כהן also cuts every thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from the word 'פרע' here and 'פרע' by a נזיר. Here it says, 'They shall not shave their heads, nor let their hair (פרע) grow long.' There it says, 'He shall be holy, he shall let the hair (פרע) of his head grow.' Just as there it is thirty days, so too here it is thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה, linking two פסוקים that share the word 'פרע.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: By a כהן, the פסוק says not to let the hair ('פרע') grow long. By a נזיר, 'פרע' means growth of thirty days. So 'growing long' for a כהן means thirty days, and he must cut his hair by then.

keyTerms.meaning: it is learned (through a link between words)
a person who takes a vow not to cut his hair, among other rules
just as there, so too here

steps.whatToRemember: A מלך cuts daily (to be seen 'in his beauty'), a כהן גדול every Friday (for each new משמר), and a כהן הדיוט every thirty days (from the 'פרע' link to נזיר).

phrases.english: It is derived from "pera" and "pera" from a nazirite,
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word in two places teaches us that they share the same law.

phrases.english: It is written here:
"Neither shall they shave their heads, nor let their locks grow long,"
and it is written there:
"He shall be holy, he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow long,"
just as there it is thirty,
phrases.notes: A plain נזירות with no set length lasts thirty days.

phrases.english: so too here it is thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26 with a גזירה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word 'פרע' links כהנים to נזיר; since a נזיר's growth is thirty days, a כהן cuts every thirty days.

steps.title: How do we know the thirty days for a נזיר himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a נזיר's hair growth lasts thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the נזיר himself, how do we know his growth is thirty days?
steps.whatsHappening: The previous step learned the כהן's thirty days from the נזיר. Now the גמרא asks how we know the נזיר's own number is thirty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison in Step 27 only works if the thirty days for a נזיר is already established. So the גמרא checks the base of that comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who takes a vow to avoid wine, haircuts, and contact with the dead
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And the nazir himself, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the base of the comparison used in Step 27
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a נזיר's growth period is thirty days

steps.title: A plain נזירות lasts thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה states that a נזירות with no length stated lasts thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: An unspecified נזירות lasts thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה gives the rule: if someone becomes a נזיר without saying for how long, it lasts thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the basic length of a נזירות at thirty days. That is why a נזיר's hair grows for thirty days, and why the comparison to כהנים gives thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the rule here
A נזירות taken without stating how long

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
An unspecified naziriteship is thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 28
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A plain נזירות lasts thirty days

steps.title: Where does the thirty-day rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רב מתנה's thirty-day rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source רב מתנה's rule is based on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנה stated the rule but gave no source. The גמרא wants a פסוק behind it.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of Step 29
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind the thirty-day rule

steps.title: The word 'יהיה' equals thirty
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'יהיה', and its numerical value is thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'he shall be (יהיה)', and in גימטריא that word equals thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the word 'יהיה' from the נזיר section and shows its letters add up to thirty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: י (10) + ה (5) + י (10) + ה (5) = 30. The 'being holy' of a plain נזיר is thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: The number value of a word's letters
'He shall be', a word in the פסוק about a נזיר

phrases.english: The verse states: "He shall be"
in numerical value, it is thirty.
phrases.notes: י is 10, ה is 5: 10+5+10+5 adds up to 30.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 30
steps.whatToRemember: The chain: a כהן cuts every thirty days (פרע ↔ נזיר) → a plain נזירות is thirty days → from 'יהיה' = 30.

steps.title: Maybe כהנים should not grow hair at all
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests the פסוק might mean כהנים may not grow their hair at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Maybe this is what the Torah means: they should not grow their hair at all!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the thirty-day reading. He suggests the פסוק might forbid כהנים from growing any hair at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק forbids any growth, then there is no thirty-day allowance. כהנים would have to cut constantly. This attacks the whole derivation for כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a student of אביי

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying:
They should not grow it at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק used in Step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that כהנים may grow hair up to thirty days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could be read as a total ban on any growth

steps.title: The word order shows some hair is allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows from the order of the words that כהנים may have hair but may not let it grow long.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If the Torah had written 'they shall not grow long hair', you would be right. But it says 'and hair, they shall not let grow long': so hair may exist, they just may not let it get long.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא from the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'פרע' (hair) first, as something that exists, and only then forbids letting it grow long. So some growth is allowed, and long growth is forbidden. This brings back the thirty-day measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (that it is written this way)

phrases.english: He said to him:
If it were written: "They shall not grow long hair,"
it would be as you said.
Now that it is written: "And hair they shall not let grow long,"
let there be hair,
it is only letting it grow long that they may not do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge in Step 32
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק forbids any hair growth for כהנים
steps.terutzMaskana: Hair may grow; only letting it grow long (past thirty days) is forbidden

steps.title: Then כהנים should keep this rule even today
steps.stepSummary: If the haircut rule comes from the Torah, כהנים should keep it even nowadays.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even today too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: if this is a Torah rule for כהנים, why don't they cut their hair every thirty days even today?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the rule is shown to come from a פסוק, it seems it should apply at all times. But כהנים today do not keep it. The challenge forces the גמרא to define when the rule applies.

phrases.english: If so,
even nowadays as well!
phrases.notes: He means כהנים today should also cut their hair every thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the Torah source in Step 33 to raise a practical problem
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that כהנים today do not keep the thirty-day haircut
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah rule should apply even when there is no מקדש

steps.title: Like the wine ban, it applies only when serving
steps.stepSummary: The haircut rule is like the ban on wine: it applies only when entering the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like those who drank wine. A כהן who drank wine is forbidden only when entering the מקדש; when not entering, it is allowed. Here too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by comparing the haircut rule to the rule of a כהן who drank wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on wine is not a ban on drinking. It only forbids entering the מקדש after drinking. The same is true of long hair, so with no מקדש today, there is no need to cut.

keyTerms.meaning: The time of entering the מקדש

phrases.english: It is similar to those who drank wine.
Just as those who drank wine
are forbidden only at the time of entering,
but when it is not the time of entering, it is permitted,
here too, the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 34
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The haircut rule applies at all times
steps.terutzMaskana: Like wine, the rule only matters when entering the מקדש
steps.confusionAlert: The wine rule does not forbid a כהן from drinking at all. It only forbids entering the מקדש to serve after drinking.

steps.title: רבי says כהנים may never drink wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wine comparison from רבי, who forbids כהנים from drinking wine at any time, and from אביי's remark about whose view כהנים follow today.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: רבי says, I say that כהנים are forbidden to drink wine at all times, but what can I do, since his misfortune is his advantage. And אביי said: Following whose view do כהנים drink wine nowadays?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 35 with רבי's opinion that כהנים may never drink wine. It also quotes אביי asking whose view כהנים follow when they drink today. The answer to אביי's question, and the rest of this challenge, continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 assumed that drinking wine is allowed when not entering the מקדש. רבי's words suggest the basic rule is a ban at all times, and it is relaxed only because of the מקדש's destruction. אביי's question hints that today's practice depends on one specific opinion. If so, the haircut rule might also apply today for those who disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: But was it not taught: Rabbi says:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמֵר אֲנִי כֹּהֲנִים אֲסוּרִים לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן לְעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: I say that priests are forbidden to drink wine at all times,
but what can I do,
since his misfortune is his advantage.
And Abaye said:
According to whom do priests drink wine nowadays?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wine comparison of Step 35
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that wine is allowed when not entering the מקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי holds the basic rule is a ban at all times, and אביי's question suggests today's drinking follows only one opinion. So the same could apply to haircuts.
